title: Choose the visual world
question: Bolder hand: the deal leads with Terminal Wayfinding. Keep it, take the alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Terminal Wayfinding
options.lineage: international airport sign systems: yellow overhead bands, black humanist sans
options.thesis: The ballot as a concourse: one yellow band per decision, each judge's percentile hung at monumental scale.
options.viewport: Yellow sign band holds nav and county select; each ballot judge is a white row led by a huge percentile in a black square, with a court pictogram and the next decision (Retain? see the numbers) at the edge.
options.risk: Yellow at full saturation fatigues if it leaks past wayfinding into data.

raised.raise: One reserved ink (course purple) marks your judge in every distribution and nowhere else.
Attorney and non-attorney results are hard halves in a fixed order everywhere, never merged in a chart.
Focusing a judge dims the rest of the cohort in its distribution, so one mark leads.
Hierarchy by scale contrast alone: monumental numerals against one small text size.

options.label: High-Density Mosaic
options.thesis: Every judge a ruled module with a red tab; a whole county's ballot and its statewide context on one screen.
options.viewport: Persistent two-row nav rail; a mosaic of judge modules, each with tiny score, percentile, attorney split and commission badge.
options.case: Holds clarity for researchers (nothing hidden); loses identification, voters on phones find it cramped.
options.risk: Tiny type on phones; reads as a portal rather than a guide.

options.label: Orienteering Map
options.thesis: Cohort as terrain, your judge as the purple course.
options.viewport: Contoured field with a purple control circle.
options.case: Loses both: contour reading is a skill voters lack.
options.kept: One reserved ink for the active item.

options.label: Cassette J-Card
options.thesis: Side A attorneys, side B everyone else.
options.case: Loses both: handwriting undermines numeric trust.
options.kept: Hard halves in a fixed order.

options.label: Title Card Wall
options.thesis: Judges as poster tiles in rows.
options.case: Loses both: no artwork exists, and hidden metadata defeats comparison.

options.label: Type Specimen
options.case: Loses both: sliders have no job here.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A nonpartisan voter guide, executed impeccably: white, civic blue, judge cards with score badges.
canonCard.viewport: County search, then a card per judge with a score badge and recommendation chip.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other voter guide by design.
